digest.en: The China-US summit in Beijing and the ongoing conflict fallout in the Middle East dominate this hour. Extreme weather events across the globe and humanitarian crises in Somalia and DR Congo also register. These stories highlight interconnected challenges from diplomacy to climate.
digest.hi: संयुक्त राष्ट्र की प्रभावशीलता पर जयशंकर की टिप्पणी और ब्रिक्स की बैठक में इसकी भूमिका पर जोर, वैश्विक कूटनीति में बहुपक्षीय संस्थानों की निरंतर प्रासंगिकता को रेखांकित करता है। अदानी परिवार द्वारा अमेरिकी जुर्माना भरने की तैयारी और माइली की कूटनीति अर्जेंटीना में क्षेत्रीय तनाव को दर्शाती है।

articles.title: Trump and Xi’s suits put ‘chameleon effect’ to test in Beijing
articles.summary: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping wore strikingly similar blue suits during their Mirroring of each other’s attire may signal alignment – though the look wasn’t a huge departure for either leaderWhen Donald Trump and Xi Jinping met for a welcome ceremony in Tiananmen Square this week with the world’s gaze on them, they mirrored one another in strikingly similar suits. Both were blue, single-breasted with flap pockets.

articles.title: Somalia at ‘real risk of famine’ as Middle East war fallout continues
articles.summary: UN aid teams warned Somalia faces a real risk of famine. At least six million people in Somalia are going days without enough food, UN aid teams warned on Friday, highlighting that nearly two million of this number are young children “at high risk of illness or death”.

articles.title: Trump-Xi accord on Iran elusive as US president’s China trip winds down
articles.summary: Donald Trump stated the US and China share similar views on ending the war in China calls for ceasefire and opening of seaway, while Donald Trump says Xi feels ‘very similar’ about ending the war in IranTrump in China – latest updatesDonald Trump has claimed that the US and China “feel very similar” about ending the war in Iran but offered no details about a possible breakthrough. The US president was speaking alongside Xi Jinping of China at the Zhongnanhai garden in Beijin.

articles.title: Furnace Creek sizzles as snow sweeps Siberia in a week of extremes
articles.summary: Honduras recorded its all-time May maximum temperature twice this month. Record heat in North and Central America coincides with egg-sized hailstones in eastern ChinaExtreme weather across several parts of the world this week has brought record-breaking temperatures to Honduras, North America and Indonesia. Honduras smashed its all-time May maximum temperature record earlier this month – only for it to be broken again on 13 May in Choluteca, known as the furnace of Cent.

articles.title: CIA director has met officials in Havana for talks, Cuba claims
articles.summary: CIA Director John Ratcliffe met Cuban officials in Havana. The Cuban government stated the meeting aimed to improve dialogue. This occurred amid complex bilateral relations between the two countries. CIA director has met officials in Havana for talks, Cuba claims.

articles.summary: U. S. President Trump arrived in Beijing for high-stakes talks with Xi Jinping. Security is heightened as trade, AI, and the war in Iran are set to dominate the summit. The leaders aim to improve the bilateral relationship.

articles.title: Foreign student fee hikes in France trigger backlash
articles.summary: France's government will increase university tuition fees for students from A French government plan to charge students from outside the EU 16 times more than previously have stoked discontent. But how does this compare to the rest of Europe, both inside the EU and out?

articles.title: HIV prevention and treatment services faltering, warns UNAIDS
articles.summary: UNAIDS warned that HIV prevention and treatment services are faltering. Decades of gains in the fight against AIDS are under growing threat as donor funding declines and community-based health services collapse in some of the world’s most vulnerable countries, the head of the joint UN programme on HIV/AIDS warned on Thursday.

articles.title: Malnutrition in Somalia, hunger crisis in DR Congo, energy shortages in Cuba
articles.summary: UN-backed food security experts warned nearly six million people in Nearly six million people in Somalia – almost a third of the population analysed – are projected to face acute hunger between April and June, with 1.9 million expected to experience emergency levels, UN-backed food security experts warned on Thursday.

articles.title: UN welcomes $1.8 billion US boost for humanitarian operations
articles.summary: The United States announced $1.8 billion in new humanitarian funding. This boost will support United Nations and partner aid operations globally. The funding arrives as rising needs and shortfalls force agencies to reduce assistance. An additional $1.8 billion in US humanitarian funding will allow the United Nations and its partners to expand emergency relief operations reaching millions of people worldwide, as rising global needs and funding shortfalls force aid agencies to scale back assistance.

articles.title: Yemen parties agree under UN mediation to release 1,600 detainees
articles.summary: Yemen's warring parties agreed to release over 1,600 detainees. The deal was brokered by the United Nations in Jordan. This marks the largest prisoner exchange since the civil war began. The agreement offers a rare sign of progress in stalled peace efforts. More than 1,600 conflict-related detainees in Yemen will be released under a UN-brokered agreement reached after months of negotiations in Jordan, marking the largest prisoner release deal since the country’s civil war began and offering a rare sign of progress in stalled peace efforts.

articles.title: UN pleads for Equatorial Guinea not to send US asylum seekers to their home countries: ‘Their life
articles.summary: United Nations human rights experts publicly urged Equatorial Guinea to stop returning US deportees. The experts cited reports of political violence, torture, and death faced by individuals sent back to their home countries. Deportees described being held in prison-like conditions.

articles.title: WHO says hantavirus ship operation completed, monitoring to continue
articles.summary: The international operation to disembark and repatriate passengers from the hantavirus A complex international operation to disembark and repatriate passengers from the hantavirus-hit MV Hondius has concluded in Tenerife, with the World Health Organization (WHO) praising Spain’s leadership while warning that global coordination must continue in the weeks ahead.

articles.title: In Addis Ababa, Guterres urges reforms to give Africa stronger global voice
articles.summary: United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres stated in Addis Ababa that Africa's growing influence is hampered by outdated global institutions and costly borrowing. He spoke as the UN and the African Union renewed their strategic partnership. Guterres called for reforms to ensure Africa has a more significant voice on the global stage.

articles.title: Funding shortfalls force deep cuts to Syria food assistance: WFP
articles.summary: The UN World Food Programme halved emergency food assistance in Syria. Millions of Syrians are at growing risk of hunger after severe funding shortages forced the UN World Food Programme (WFP) to halve emergency food assistance, cutting support for hundreds of thousands of vulnerable people across the country.

articles.title: ‘Blatant disregard for rights’: concern grows over Gabon’s social media clampdown
articles.summary: Gabon's media regulator suspended major social media platforms indefinitely in February. The regulator cited security concerns during anti-government protests. This action has led to increased use of Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) to bypass restrictions. Activists claim these laws curtail internet freedoms. This is part of a history of cracking down on dissent.

articles.title: इस्राइल और लेबनान के बीच तीसरे दौर की वार्ता खत्म, अमेरिका बोला- सकारात्मक रही बैठक
articles.summary: इस्राइल और लेबनान के बीच समुद्री सीमा विवाद पर तीसरे दौर की वार्ता अमेरिका की मध्यस्थता में समाप्त हुई। अमेरिकी विदेश विभाग ने बैठक को सकारात्मक बताया। दोनों देशों के प्रतिनिधियों ने लेबनान के दक्षिणी तट पर स्थित रास अल-नाकुरा में मुलाकात की। यह वार्ता दोनों देशों के बीच लंबे समय से चले आ रहे सीमा विवाद को सुलझाने की दिशा में एक महत्वपूर्ण कदम है।

articles.title: यूएई और ईरान के मंत्री नई दिल्ली में बैठक के दौरान आपस में भिड़े, जानिए पूरा मामला
articles.summary: नई दिल्ली में ब्रिक्स विदेश मंत्रियों की बैठक के दौरान ईरान और संयुक्त अरब अमीरात के मंत्रियों के बीच तीखी बहस हुई। यह घटनाक्रम तब हुआ जब इजरायल ने नेतन्याहू के यूएई दौरे की घोषणा की। नई दिल्ली में ईरान और यूएई के मंत्री ब्रिक्स देशों के विदेश मंत्रियों की बैठक के दौरान आपस में भिड़ गए.
